title: The Studio Pivot: Why I Stopped Selling AI and Started Fixing the Internet
summary: A look back at the evolution of Minescout—from a sandbox testing ground to an AI widget vendor, and finally to a managed digital agency focusing on serverless Clean Slate Rebuilds.
content:
March 2025: The Sandbox and Minescout Life

The journey started in the spring of 2025 with life.minescout.net and beta.minescout.net. At the time, minescout.net wasn't an agency or a business. It was just a sandbox. I was a high school freshman obsessed with how the internet worked, testing emerging Large Language Models, and documenting early AI-assisted workflows.

I realized pretty quickly that just having a GitHub profile wasn't enough to explain complex engineering or AI concepts to non-technical people. I needed a platform to show my work.

Early 2026: The Dual Tracks & The 17-Day Sprint

By early 2026, I started taking on actual client work, beginning the overhaul for chop-lab.com alongside developing my own core technology. I was initially managing these projects as completely separate, static codebases. It took about a week to realize this was entirely unscalable. Fixing a bug on one site meant manually deploying it across all of them.

In March 2026, I initiated a 17-day sprint to tear down the static infrastructure and build a central, multi-tenant SaaS edge router using Cloudflare Workers and KV storage. I was building a single "brain" that could serve multiple clients simultaneously at the network edge.

Summer 2026: The "Minescout AI" Illusion

With the edge router live, I launched the first commercial iteration of minescout.net as a standalone product: Minescout AI. The goal was to sell custom, context-aware AI support agents to local Sammamish businesses to automate their FAQs and lead capture.

Then I hit a massive reality check. I discovered the fatal flaw in the business model: trying to integrate a lightning-fast, highly advanced AI widget into sluggish, 10-year-old legacy WordPress sites.

It's like trying to put a V8 sports car engine into a rusted, broken chassis. It doesn't win the race. Local businesses didn't just need an AI widget; their underlying digital infrastructure was fundamentally broken.

The Chop Lab Epiphany

I took a step back and looked closely at why the chop-lab.com v2 rebuild was so successful. It wasn't just about the AI capabilities; it was the Custom Single Page Application (SPA) architecture.

The real value was the decoupled data model—the "Backstage" portal. The client loved being able to easily update product specs and gallery images through a custom form without ever touching code or dealing with a bloated CMS. The actual valuable product wasn't the AI widget. The product was the Clean Slate Rebuild—throwing out the tech debt and delivering a sub-second, serverless edge application. The AI was just the ultimate premium bolt-on.

October 2026: The Studio Pivot

In October 2026, I officially transitioned the platform to minescout.net/studio. I shifted from a software vendor trying to sell a widget to a digital agency providing fully managed infrastructure.

  • The Custodian Model: Clients own their IP and domains, but I manage 100% of the edge hosting, security, and deployments. They never have to stress about broken plugins again.
  • The AI Site Builder: To solve the client discovery bottleneck, I launched the new AI Site Builder tool on minescout.net/studio. It lets an autonomous AI agent chat with prospects to generate project specs directly from the site.

Where It Goes From Here

The mission moving forward is simple: technology should get out of the user's way. Whether I am building a portfolio or an automated customer service tool, the goal is a seamless, zero-maintenance experience for the client.

Scaling this managed agency model on minescout.net while actively balancing 10th-grade UW Precalc, Den Chief responsibilities, and the FRC 1294 trial period is going to be the next great challenge. But with the edge routing locked in and the infrastructure humming, the foundation is finally ready.

  This post documents the real architectural pivot of Minescout Studio. The codebases, the 17-day sprints, and the realization that good AI requires good infrastructure are all genuine lessons learned at the edge.
